concepts.title: The Sociological Imagination: Personal Trouble as Public Issue
concepts.definition: Sociology teaches us to see private experiences as connected to public arrangements: one person's joblessness is a biography, but mass joblessness is a fact about the economy and society. This way of linking personal biography to social structure is the sociological imagination that the discipline offers its students.
concepts.key_idea: Look behind any individual fate for the social arrangement that produces it -- biography meets history in society.
concepts.textbook_ref: kesy101.txt lines 1-120 (introduction, unemployment example, individual and society, sociological perspective linking personal and public)
question_patterns: what is the sociological imagination
in class 11 sociology and society: how does sociology connect personal troubles to public issues
explain the unemployment example to show the sociological perspective
why is sociology said to look behind common sense
distinguish a personal trouble from a public issue with an example
how does biography connect with social structure

solution_steps.explain: Begin with an individual situation -- losing a job, failing an exam -- which looks like personal failure.
Ask how many others share the situation and what institutions -- markets, schools, laws -- shape their chances.
When a private difficulty reflects the working of social arrangements, it becomes a public issue sociology can study.

worked_examples.q: Mass joblessness, unlike one person's joblessness, is a fact about what?

concepts.title: The Emergence of Sociology in Europe
concepts.definition: Sociology was born in nineteenth-century Europe from three upheavals: the French Revolution's promise and turbulence in politics, the industrial revolution's factories and cities in economy, and the growth of science as a model of knowledge. Thinkers sought new ways to understand a society that tradition no longer explained.
concepts.key_idea: Revolution created the modern world and, to explain it, a new science of society.
concepts.textbook_ref: kesy101.txt lines 120-240 (emergence of sociology, french revolution, industrial revolution, growth of natural science as model, enlightenment)
question_patterns: how did the french and industrial revolutions give birth to sociology
in class 11 sociology and society: why did sociology emerge in nineteenth century europe
what role did the enlightenment play in the rise of sociology
how did urbanisation and factory life create questions for early sociologists
why did social thinkers imitate the natural sciences
connect modernity with the origin of sociology

solution_steps.explain: The French Revolution overthrew inherited order and raised questions of rights, citizenship and change that demanded study.
Industrialisation built factories, cities and a wage-earning class, generating slums, poverty and new inequalities to explain.
The prestige of natural science encouraged thinkers to seek laws of society, founding sociology as a science of the social.

worked_examples.q: In which century was sociology born in Europe?

concepts.title: Sociology in India: Colonial Encounter and Native Traditions
concepts.definition: Sociology in India grew from a double source: the colonial administration's need to know the people it governed -- producing censuses, ethnographies and caste surveys -- and India's own traditions of social and religious inquiry. After independence the discipline turned to studying Indian society with Indian purposes: nation-building, development and reform.
concepts.key_idea: Indian sociology carries a colonial archive and a native curiosity -- it was shaped both by rulers' questions and by India's own.
concepts.textbook_ref: kesy101.txt lines 240-360 (sociology in india, colonial influence, indology, census and ethnography, growth after independence, indian traditions of social thought)
question_patterns: how did colonialism shape the growth of sociology in india
in class 11 sociology and society: what is the indological approach to indian society
why did the colonial government conduct censuses and ethnographic studies
how did indian traditions of thought contribute to sociology
distinguish the colonial and nationalist phases of indian sociology
what questions did sociologists take up after independence

solution_steps.explain: Administrative needs produced censuses, gazetteers and caste ethnographies, creating data and categories about Indian society.
Sanskritic and textual traditions, reform movements and thinkers supplied home-grown accounts of social life.
Universities after 1947 built an Indian sociology addressing village studies, caste, tribe and development for India's own purposes.

worked_examples.q: Which colonial exercise counted castes ten-yearly from 1881?

concepts.title: Sociology, Economics, Political Science and History: Distinct but Related
concepts.definition: Sociology shares subject matter with sibling disciplines yet keeps its own angle: economics abstracts the market, political science the state, history the past in sequence -- while sociology studies the whole web of social relationships in which all of these are embedded, including their unspecialised everyday settings.
concepts.key_idea: Others take one thread of social life; sociology studies the whole cloth of relationships.
concepts.textbook_ref: kesy101.txt lines 360-460 (sociology and other social sciences, relation with economics political science history anthropology psychology)
question_patterns: distinguish sociology from economics political science and history
in class 11 sociology and society: how does sociology differ from anthropology and psychology
what is common to all social sciences
why is sociology called the mother of social sciences by some
give an example where sociology and economics study the same event differently
how does the sociological viewpoint differ from that of history

solution_steps.explain: All social sciences study human behaviour in society, so their borders are porous.
Economics isolates market exchange, political science power and state, history time-bound narrative -- each by deliberate abstraction.
Sociology studies the total patterns of interaction -- including the unorganised, everyday and informal -- that other disciplines' abstractions leave out.

worked_examples.q: Which discipline abstracts the market from social life?

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student says a classmate who failed the board exam simply did not work hard. Reinterpret the case sociologically.

solution_template.explain: The common-sense reading locates cause in the student's effort alone.
Ask about family income, school quality, language of instruction and work at home -- resources no single student commands.
If such disadvantages repeat across a group, failure rates reflect social structure -- the sociological imagination at work.

worked_examples.source_ref: kesy101.txt lines 360-460 (sociology and other social sciences)
worked_examples.question_pattern: Farmers protest for higher crop prices. Show how economics political science history and sociology would each study this event.

solution_template.explain: Economics examines supply, price support mechanisms and market effects of the demand.

solution_template.action: assign the political and historical readings
solution_template.explain: Political science studies the protest's pressure on government; history compares it with earlier farm movements.
Sociology studies the farmers' organisation, caste and class ties, village networks and the meaning of the protest in their social world.
